title: Rye Print Show 2026
venue: Rye Creative Centre, New Road, Rye
summary: An exhibition of contemporary printmaking at the Rye Creative Centre, featuring more than 25 artists and a private view for everyone on 20 November.

title: Robertsbridge Bonfire
summary: The town's procession moves through the High Street to end at the recreation ground, where a giant bonfire is lit and fireworks follow.

title: Christmas Tree Festival: artisan fair
summary: An artisan fair with refreshments as part of Battle's Christmas Tree Festival.

title: Hastings Christmas Designer Maker Fair
venue: The Observer Building, Cambridge Road, Hastings
summary: The yearly Christmas market, with over 50 designers, makers and craft makers selling across textiles, stationery, gifts, home and food and drink. It runs on Saturday 21 November and Sunday 22 November, 10am to 4pm, at The Observer Building.

title: Winchelsea Christmas Fair
venue: The New Hall, Rectory Lane, Winchelsea
summary: A fair with stalls from local artisans, a grand raffle, tombola and refreshments. Proceeds are divided between the Rye Food Bank and The New Hall Charity; entry is £1, free under 16s.

title: Henry V by William Shakespeare
summary: The Bard's history of King Henry V's invasion of France and the Battle of Agincourt, staged in the Dukes Library at Battle Abbey.

title: Paleo Art through the Lens of the Magic Lantern workshop
venue: Hastings Museum and Art Gallery, Bohemia Road, Hastings
summary: Hastings Museum and Art Gallery, in collaboration with Theatre Rotto and supported by the Geologists' Association, is presenting events in November exploring the relationship between Gideon and Mary Ann Mantell of Lewes and the geologist Charles Lyell. Keith Leech will introduce the session on how the Victorians came to comprehend deep time, and participants will create their own magic lantern slides.

title: Amuse Bouche comedy writing taster
venue: Downstairs bar, White Rock Hotel, Hastings
summary: A female-powered introductory workshop in comedy writing, ad libbing, improv and flash fiction, run by Lindsay Jayne, Nicky Torode, Nicola Reading and Stella Valente. No experience needed, just a sense of humour.
